reading.body:
Avoma is a meeting intelligence platform that automates sales tasks like note-taking and CRM entry, claiming users save over four hours weekly through AI-powered conversation analytics and coaching.

The company operates in the notes, knowledge, and meetings category, which sits upstream of compute requirements by generating structured data from unstructured conversations. Sales teams generate enormous volumes of call recordings and meeting transcripts, all requiring storage, processing, and indexing. A platform that extracts patterns from this data and surfaces actionable alerts creates continuous demand for inference capacity.

Avoma's feature set, centered on conversation analytics and risk detection, depends on running language models repeatedly across call recordings and transcripts. Each meeting analyzed requires compute to tokenize, embed, score, and generate coaching recommendations. As revenue teams grow and meeting volumes increase, per-user compute consumption likely grows as well, making this category relevant to overall AI infrastructure demand.

The data does not cover Avoma's architecture, infrastructure partners, or whether it operates its own models or relies on third-party APIs. California's regulatory environment affects all software companies headquartered there, but the 181 legal exposure records in the dataset cannot be evaluated without case details. No information about the company's scale, deployment model, or data residency is available.

profile_text.body:
Avoma is an AI platform for note-taking, scheduling, and coaching headquartered in Fremont, California. The company describes its product as an all-in-one platform that automates note-taking, scheduling, call coaching, CRM updates, and other tasks, with a pricing model where customers pay only for what they need.

The platform targets revenue teams with meeting intelligence and conversation analytics capabilities. According to the company's site, Avoma saves users 4+ hours per week by automating note-taking, email follow-ups, and CRM data entry. It offers features including an AI Copilot for objective answers, automated scheduling and lead qualification, call scoring and personalized coaching to increase win rates, and AI-driven deal risk alerts and win-loss analysis to improve forecasting and quota attainment. The company provides setup assistance and team training without extra fees during and after trial periods.

Avoma operates in a high-regulation environment, with 208 known cases connected to California law exposure.
